subject: Private Offer: CloudScale reseller uplift mechanics + list-price floor check
content:
From: Laura Gomez <laura@cloudscalepartners.com>

Cc: procurement@nimbleanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudScale / Nimble — private offer mechanics and channel uplift questions

Hi Mina —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Nimble procurement asked a few concrete questions we need clarified before CloudScale presents the private offer pricing:

- Does Redwood require a list-price floor on the AWS private offer for reseller uplift to be applied? If so, is there a minimum (e.g., 1.1x or 1.2x list)?
- Can CloudScale apply a percentage uplift (reseller margin) inside the private offer, or does the uplift need to be handled as a separate pass-through billing line?
- How do pass-through credits / early-adopter credits show up in Redwood reporting vs marketplace invoices? Nimble needs the invoice flow for their accounting team.

Attached: CloudScale_Terms_v2.pdf, Nimble_Spend_Snapshot.xlsx

Appreciate any quick guidance — Nimble wants to present an updated offer to their finance team by next Monday.

Best,
Laura Gomez\Channel Partnerships, CloudScale

On Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 11:05 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: CloudScale / Nimble — private offer mechanics and channel uplift questions

Hi Laura — thanks for the details and the spend snapshot. Looping in Ben and Irene (marketplace ops / channel) — they can confirm the ops model and the invoice flows. Jordan, can you keep billing in the loop?

Quick answers up front:
- Redwood does not *mandate* a specific list-price floor, but AWS Marketplace private offers often require a list price to be set on the SKU(s). In practice we recommend a list-price floor at ~1.2x the effective Redwood list for private-offer pass-through uplifts so partner margin doesn’t push the sale price below Marketplace pricing guardrails.
- Two practical models are common:
  1) Reseller uplift baked into private-offer price (single marketplace invoice to Nimble; CloudScale gets settlement from AWS).
  2) Reseller uplift handled outside of the marketplace via separate partner invoice (CloudScale invoices Nimble directly for the margin).

Which you pick affects Nimble’s accounting (single invoice vs split). If Nimble prefers one invoice we can support the baked-in option, but CloudScale needs to set the private-offer list price high enough to absorb the margin and any passbacks.

I attached our private-offer playbook to illustrate examples.

Next: Ben / Irene — can you sketch the recommended uplift % and confirm any marketplace SKU naming constraints for the list-price approach? Also confirm whether we need any special DocuSign language for the private-offer attachment.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad\Head of Sales, Americas\Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-private-offer-playbook.pdf (pdf, 312 KB)]

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 08:30 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Gomez <laura@cloudscalepartners.com>, procurement@nimbleanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: CloudScale / Nimble — private offer mechanics and channel uplift questions

Folks — quick ops breakdown based on the spend snapshot and our prior deals with similar partners. Keeping things practical to get Nimble signed this quarter: 

Option A — Baked-in private offer (recommended for simplicity):
- Private offer list price = Redwood list * 1.20 (example: $0.50 token price -> $0.60 list in offer).
- Marketplace invoice to Nimble shows the $0.60 line; AWS settles to CloudScale (per AWS settlement). CloudScale then remits the Redwood net per contract (we reconcile in payout).
- Pros: single invoice for Nimble; simple procurement acceptance.
- Cons: CloudScale needs to manage currency of settlement timing and potential AWS fees.

Option B — Pass-through margin outside marketplace:
- Private offer price = Redwood list (no uplift). CloudScale invoices Nimble separately for the margin (e.g., 15% uplift on usage).
- Pros: Faster settlements to Redwood; clearer separation of product vs partner services.
- Cons: Two invoices for Nimble (can slow procurement).

Recommended uplift: 12–18% range depending on account complexity. For Nimble's volume snapshot I recommend 15% uplift (this keeps list-price floor at 1.15–1.20x; see attached quick calc).

Important ops notes:
- SKU naming: keep SKU suffix ":CS" for partner offers to make billing rollups easier.
- Credits: Early-adopter or promotional credits should be configured as separate line items (not buried in per-token price) so Nimble's finance can map credits to P&L correctly.
- Tax / passthroughs: need CloudScale to confirm VAT/tax handling; we can align on invoice language.

Attachment: quick_calc_sample.txt (inline)

Sample calculation (illustrative):
- Redwood list per 1k tokens = $0.50
- Private-offer list @ 1.20 = $0.60
- Usage month = 10M tokens -> $6,000 invoice to Nimble
- CloudScale uplift (15%) -> effective CloudScale margin = $900 (either baked in or billed separately)

If we go with Option A, Jordan — operationally we'll need the marketplace SKU mapping and an expected settlement cadence (AWS pays monthly; CloudScale may receive funds before/after we do netting). Jordan, can you confirm our payout path and any timing mismatch risks?

-Ben
Senior Channel Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final wording & next steps — CloudScale private offer for Nimble

Hi Laura / Nimble team —

Thanks — below is the final recommended language and the operational checklist to move to DocuSign. We captured the baked-in model (Option A) since CloudScale confirmed preference.

Marketplace invoice wording (suggested):
- Redwood Inference — LLM Inference (tokens) — Private Offer (CloudScale partner price)
  SKU: RDW-INFR-LLM:CS
  Unit: per 1,000 tokens
  Price: $0.60 per 1k tokens (private-offer list price)

Early-adopter credit formatting:
- Reference credit as a separate invoice line: "Early Adopter Credit — Redwood Inference" with negative amount. This is standard practice and AWS marketplace will display negative line items if configured as promotional credits on the offer. 

Channel uplift treatment (as implemented):
- Private-offer list price above reflects a 15% reseller uplift over Redwood list. CloudScale will receive settlement from AWS according to their settlement agreement; Redwood will reconcile net revenues with CloudScale during monthly payout.

Operational checklist (what each party needs to do):
- CloudScale: confirm final list-price(s) and provide preferred SKUs and currency (USD).
- Nimble procurement: confirm acceptance of invoice wording and that a single marketplace invoice is acceptable.
- Redwood (Ben/Jordan/Irene): publish the private-offer in AWS and add SKU suffix ":CS" for partner tracking. Set promotional credit line to be shown as negative line item.
- Signed DocuSign: pending (link below).

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/ABC123-CloudScale-Offer (placeholder)
